definitions.explanation: A small pocket of air or gas trapped in a liquid, solid, or other material. Used in both everyday and scientific contexts.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}の{中|なか}に{気泡|きほう}ができた。
ガラスの{中|なか}に{小|ちい}さな{気泡|きほう}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: You can see small air bubbles inside the glass.

examples.japanese: コンクリートに{気泡|きほう}が{入|はい}ると{強度|きょうど}が{下|さ}がるので{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: If air bubbles get into concrete, the strength decreases, so care is needed.

notes:
Refers specifically to bubbles of air or gas, whether in liquids, solids, or materials. More precise and technical than {泡|あわ}, which is the general word for foam or bubbles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {気泡|きほう}が{入|はい}る — for air bubbles to get in
- {気泡|きほう}ができる — for bubbles to form
- {気泡|きほう}を{取|と}り{除|のぞ}く — to remove air bubbles
- {気泡|きほう}{緩衝材|かんしょうざい} — bubble wrap (bubble cushioning material)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {泡|あわ} — bubble, foam; the everyday general word for bubbles, including soap bubbles and foam on beer
- {水泡|すいほう} — water bubble; also used figuratively in {水泡|すいほう}に{帰|き}する (to come to nothing)
- {泡沫|うたかた} — ephemeral bubble; literary word suggesting something fleeting
